title: Equality and rigidity in the spacetime Penrose inequality
main_claim: If equality m = F_n(a(g)) holds for outermost, outer-area-minimizing initial data that satisfy the dominant energy condition, then (g,K) is the induced data of a slice of a Schwarzschild–Tangherlini exterior, smoothly attached to the future horizon or the bifurcation sphere. This holds for all n>=3 under strong decay, and for n=3 and n=4 under weak decay. In n=3, a disconnected horizon forces the strict inequality m > sqrt(A/16pi).
coverage:
Third pass. Two earlier sibling passes already reported no_gap_found on the variational, separation, static-base, 3D-global and 4D routes. This pass covered the section they left unchecked: three/05-local-spinor, the alternative local-spinor proof of the two-sphere strictness. I checked it line by line:
- The conformal family q_t=((1+t lambda)/(1+t))^4 h is scalar flat and complete for t<1.
- The end expansion (q_t)_ij=(1+2a(t-1)/((1+t)r))delta holds; in the Schwarzschild case q_* is flat.
- The spin-structure argument and the Lichnerowicz identity for C^2 metrics hold.
- The ray Hardy inequality (constant 4, favorable inner boundary term) and the anchored Poincare inequality are uniform in t.
- The Dirac isometry/projection argument holds, and the L^2 harmonic residual vanishes by the cutoff argument plus infinite end volume.
- The Witten-type flux estimate |B(psi0,psi0)|<=C((1-t)+R^{1-2q0}) holds.
- The weighted Hardy bound keeps the limit spinor nonzero; a parallel spinor gives Ric=0, hence flat in 3D.
- The conformal second fundamental form is II_{q*}=8 kappa q*. Gauss-Bonnet then gives |S_i|_g = pi/kappa^2 = 16 pi m^2 for each sphere, which contradicts equality.
I also re-checked c = 16pi dm/dA = 1/(2m) and kappa = c/2 = 1/(4m) from the free-boundary variation. From the strong-class recovery I re-checked:
- the filled-double inverted-point W^{2,s} exponents (n/2<s<n/(2-eta), p>2s);
- the seam umbilic curvature 2^{2/(n-2)} 2kappa/(n-2);
- the isotropic solution M=2R0^{n-2} and A=omega(2M)^{k/(k-1)} => M=m;
- the tortoise and Kruskal smoothness.
I did not re-derive the PDE regularity, the n>=8 singular-sheet analysis, or the rough-mass lemmas (the latter rest on companion Riemannian Thm 1.1).
